question: Does Ramapo have a 4+1 program where I can get a masters in 5 years in a STEM field? which ones?
answer:
Yes. The catalog lists these STEM-related 4+1 programs [6]:
- Applied Mathematics 4+1 (Bachelor of Science): students in Computer Science BS, Data Science BS, and Mathematics BS are eligible; students with other bachelor’s degrees may contact the Graduate Program Director about a 5-year plan. It allows completion of the MS in Applied Mathematics in one additional year after the 4-year bachelor’s degree. [1]
- Computer Science 4+1 (Bachelor of Science): students in Computer Science BS, Data Science BS, and Mathematics BS are eligible; students with other bachelor’s degrees may contact the Graduate Program Director about a 5-year plan. It allows completion of the MS in Computer Science in one additional year after the 4-year bachelor’s degree. [2]
The catalog also lists Data Science 4+1, but the provided pages do not describe its eligibility or timeline. [6]

question: What should a freshman math major take first semester? calc 1 right away or something else
answer:
Mathematics is offered as a BS major [1]. The pages don’t give a current freshman’s exact first-semester schedule or say that every Mathematics major should start in Calculus I; the placement score determines the calculus-track course. If you plan to take MATH 121 Calculus I, you must take the Calculus Placement Test before registering [11]. The test assesses material from intermediate algebra through pre-calculus [4].

Use the Advanced Algebra and Functions score on your report: 280–300 places you in MATH 121, MATH 237, or MATH 205; 260–279 in MATH 110 Pre-Calculus; 200–259 in MATH 024 [8]. MATH 024 is non-credit-bearing and prepares you for Pre-Calculus; MATH 110/121/122/237 are college-level calculus-track courses [2]. A score of 3 on AP Calculus AB or BC allows you to register for MATH 121 without the placement test, but gives no credit. AP Calculus AB score 4 or 5 gives credit for Calculus I; BC score 4 or 5 gives credit for Calculus I and II, and both exempt you from the placement test [4].

For help interpreting your placement or deciding your schedule, contact the Testing Center: testing@ramapo.edu, (201) 684-7441 [4].

Sources: [1](https://catalog.ramapo.edu/programs) [2](https://www.ramapo.edu/testing/post-testing/) [4](https://www.ramapo.edu/testing/calculus/) [8](https://www.ramapo.edu/testing/math-placement/) [11](https://catalog.ramapo.edu/pages/R532kjMfIcfnIkM0srb3#basic-skills-placement-testing-exemption1)

question: bio 2nd year sequence - when do you take genetics vs cell bio and are there prereqs for each
answer:
The published schedule is for Biology: Ramapo/NYCPM 3+4 Podiatry, for students admitted in 2026–2027: Genetics is in second-year fall; Cell & Molecular Biology is in third-year fall, not second year. [1]

Genetics (BIOL 332 lecture and BIOL 332L lab): prerequisites are one of BIOL 112; BIOL 113 and BIOL 113L; BIOL 215; or BIOL 216 and BIOL 216L; plus one of CHEM 110 or CHEM 116 and CHEM 116L; and CRWT 102 or CRWT 102S. Enroll in the lab with the lecture, and the lecture with the lab. [2][4]

Cell & Molecular Biology (BIOL 407 lecture): prerequisites are one of BIOL 331 or BIOL 332 and BIOL 332L; one of CHEM 205, CHEM 206 and CHEM 206L, CHEM 212, or CHEM 213 and CHEM 213L; and CRWT 102 or CRWT 102S. Enroll in BIOL 407L with the lecture. [3]

Sources: [1](https://catalog.ramapo.edu/programs/SN-BS-BIOL) [2](https://catalog.ramapo.edu/courses/BIOL332) [3](https://catalog.ramapo.edu/courses/BIOL407) [4](https://catalog.ramapo.edu/courses/BIOL332L)
